V5 CHARACTER CREATION — ALWAYS LOADED REFERENCE

A V5 player-character is built within the chronicle's frame: chronicle mode, city, Tenets, antagonist tier, coterie structure. Character creation operates after session zero establishes the chronicle frame (see vtm_v5_chronicle_creation.json). Building a character before the chronicle is established produces characters that don't fit the chronicle they end up in.

ORDER OF OPERATIONS (kit standard):

1. CONCEPT — what this kindred is, in one or two sentences. Includes mortal past, Embrace circumstance, current driving force, role in coterie.
2. CLAN — one of 16 kit-supported clans. Clan defines Bane, Compulsion, in-clan Disciplines, sect-political baseline.
3. ATTRIBUTES — Physical, Social, Mental scores via priority distribution.
4. SKILLS — skill ratings via priority distribution plus three specialties (one mandatory for Academics / Craft / Performance / Science).
5. DISCIPLINES — two dots in in-clan Disciplines (or per Predator Type for Caitiff / Thin-Blood).
6. PREDATOR TYPE — feeding methodology shaping skill bonuses, Discipline bonus, starting Advantages, starting Flaws.
7. GENERATION AND BLOOD POTENCY — generational depth and starting Blood Potency.
8. TOUCHSTONES AND CONVICTIONS — 1-3 Touchstones tied to 1-3 Convictions, with full Touchstone details.
9. AMBITION AND DESIRE — longer-arc goal and session-or-arc want.
10. ADVANTAGES — Backgrounds, Merits, Flaws; Advantages (positive) and Flaws (negative) balanced per kit standard.
11. DERIVED STATS — Health, Willpower, Humanity, starting Hunger.
12. APPEARANCE AND HISTORY — physical description, mortal past detail, Embrace details, sire identity and relationship.
13. FINALIZATION — sheet review, coterie integration check, chronicle-frame fit confirmation.

This lorebook covers each step in detail across entries 1-15:
- Entry 1: Order of operations and priority distribution
- Entry 2: Concept and core idea
- Entry 3: Clan selection (all 16 kit clans)
- Entry 4: Attributes
- Entry 5: Skills and specialties
- Entry 6: Starting Disciplines
- Entry 7: Predator Types
- Entry 8: Generation and Blood Potency
- Entry 9: Touchstones, Convictions, Ambition, Desire
- Entry 10: Advantages — Backgrounds, Merits, Flaws
- Entry 11: Derived stats — Health, Willpower, Humanity, Hunger
- Entry 12: Appearance, history, sire
- Entry 13: Kit-specific character creation notes per chronicle mode
- Entry 14: AI narrator character creation protocol
- Entry 15: Character sheet finalization and coterie integration

KIT BASELINE ASSUMPTIONS:

- Default Generation: 12th-13th for neonate PCs in most chronicles; 11th for established-coterie chronicles; 10th rare and chronicle-shaping.
- Default Blood Potency: 1 for neonate PCs (12th-13th gen); 2 for 11th gen; higher only at Storyteller approval.
- Default starting Humanity: 7 for most concepts; 6 for darker-concept PCs; 8 for Touchstone-rich concepts at Storyteller approval.
- Default starting Hunger: 1 for chronicle-start sessions; modified per Predator Type and last-fed circumstance.
- All clans are available unless chronicle mode restricts (Sabbat-survivor chronicles favor Lasombra, Tzimisce, Banu Haqim antitribu-tradition; Camarilla orthodox chronicles favor Ventrue, Toreador, Tremere, Malkavian, Nosferatu, Brujah; Anarch Movement chronicles favor Brujah, Gangrel, Caitiff, Thin-Blood with all others present; Hecata chronicles require Hecata clan).

When creating a new V5 character, work through entries 1-15 in order, surfacing each component explicitly. Skipping steps produces mechanically-incomplete or thematically-incoherent characters that strain at the chronicle's first stress-test.

1.content:
ORDER OF OPERATIONS AND PRIORITY DISTRIBUTION

V5 character creation uses priority distribution: the player assigns priority levels (Primary / Secondary / Tertiary) to Attribute and Skill categories, with each priority level producing a specific dot-distribution pattern.

ATTRIBUTE PRIORITY:

Three Attribute categories (Physical, Social, Mental), each with three Attributes:

- Physical: Strength, Dexterity, Stamina
- Social: Charisma, Manipulation, Composure
- Mental: Intelligence, Wits, Resolve

Each Attribute starts at 1. Player assigns priority and distributes additional dots:

- PRIMARY (4 dots to distribute): produces one 4-dot Attribute, one 3-dot Attribute, one 2-dot Attribute in the category
- SECONDARY (3 dots to distribute): produces one 3-dot Attribute, two 2-dot Attributes in the category, OR one 3-dot and one 3-dot with one 1-dot
- TERTIARY (2 dots to distribute): produces one 3-dot Attribute, one 2-dot Attribute, one 1-dot Attribute in the category

Alternative readable framing per kit: Primary category produces a 4/3/2 dot Attribute split; Secondary produces 3/3/2; Tertiary produces 3/2/2.

No Attribute may start above 4 at character creation without specific Advantages or chronicle-frame exception.

SKILL PRIORITY:

Three Skill distributions (chosen by the player based on character concept):

- JACK-OF-ALL-TRADES: one 3-dot Skill, eight 2-dot Skills, ten 1-dot Skills. Broad capability, no specialty.
- BALANCED: one 3-dot Skill, three 2-dot Skills, seven 1-dot Skills, with specialties on two of those. Mid-range.
- SPECIALIST: one 4-dot Skill, three 3-dot Skills, three 2-dot Skills, three 1-dot Skills. Deep capability in narrow band.

KIT NOTE — the priority distributions match V5 core rulebook; experienced players may recognise them.

SPECIALTIES:

Three Specialties at chronicle start. One mandatory: Academics, Craft, Performance, or Science requires a Specialty if rated. (Example: a PC with Academics 2 must specify Specialty — "Forensic Pathology" or "Medieval History" or similar.) The other two Specialties are player-chosen on any Skill, including the mandatory category.

Specialties grant +1 die to relevant Skill rolls. "Brawl (Grappling)," "Firearms (Pistols)," "Larceny (Lockpicking)," "Stealth (Urban)," "Persuasion (Negotiation)," "Investigation (Crime Scenes)," "Occult (Vampire Lore)" are example formats.

DISCIPLINE STARTING DOTS:

Two dots in in-clan Disciplines:
- Two dots in one in-clan Discipline, OR
- One dot each in two in-clan Disciplines

Clan-specific in-clan Discipline lists in Entry 3. Caitiff choose any two non-Blood-Sorcery Disciplines (with Storyteller approval); Thin-Blood follow Thin-Blood Alchemy rules.

PREDATOR TYPE BONUSES:

Predator Type (Entry 7) provides additional dots:
- One Specialty (in Predator-Type-specific Skill)
- One Discipline dot (Predator-Type-specific Discipline, may extend in-clan or grant out-of-clan)
- Advantages and Flaws (Predator-Type-specific)

ADVANTAGES POINTS:

Seven dots in Advantages (Backgrounds + Merits), subject to:
- No single Advantage above 3 at character creation without Storyteller approval
- Two dots in Flaws (negative Advantages); these grant two free additional Advantage dots
- Maximum two Advantage dots from Predator Type's free choices

Effective Advantage budget at chronicle start: 7 + 2 (from Flaws) = 9 Advantage dots, minus 2 Flaw dots, with Predator Type adjustments.

FINAL STATS:

- Health = Stamina + 3
- Willpower = Composure + Resolve
- Humanity = 7 (default; adjusted per Predator Type, Touchstone richness, chronicle Tenets)
- Hunger = 1 at chronicle start (adjusted per Predator Type, last-feeding circumstance, Storyteller calibration)
- Blood Potency per Generation (Entry 8)

ORDER NOTES:

Players experienced with V5 may build in different orders; the kit's standard order produces fewest revision-loops. Concept first prevents mechanically-strong but thematically-incoherent builds. Clan after concept ensures clan choice serves the character rather than the build optimising for clan mechanics. Disciplines after Predator Type ensures Predator Type's Discipline bonus is integrated rather than wasted on duplicate dots.

KIT NOTES:

- Camarilla orthodox chronicles benefit from Specialist or Balanced skill distributions; broad-status-pursuit PCs sit at Balanced.
- Brisbane Sabbat-survivor chronicles benefit from Specialist or Balanced (cell-operational specialisation rewarded).
- Methuselah-tempo Sydney chronicles benefit from Specialist (aesthetic-or-political deep capability rewarded; Sarrasine reads competence quickly).
- Anarch Movement Footscray Crew chronicles benefit from Jack-of-All-Trades or Balanced (neighbourhood operations require breadth).
- Hecata family Calabria Branch chronicles benefit from Specialist (family-tradition specialty preserved).
- Cross-supernatural diplomatic Cress Truce chronicles benefit from Balanced (cross-splat coordination requires breadth).

2.content:
CONCEPT AND CORE IDEA

Concept is the character in one or two sentences. It captures who the kindred was, who they are now, and what drives them. Strong concepts produce strong characters; weak concepts produce builds that struggle to find their place in chronicle.

A STRONG V5 CONCEPT INCLUDES:

1. MORTAL ANCHOR — what the kindred was as a mortal. Profession, social role, relationship pattern, formative experience. Example: "A Melbourne forensic pathologist who spent twenty years documenting the deaths the system couldn't explain."

2. EMBRACE CIRCUMSTANCE — how the kindred died and was reborn. Brief but specific. Example: "Embraced by a Tremere who needed a forensic specialist who could be relied on across decades and wouldn't decay; the sire didn't ask, only chose."

3. CURRENT DRIVING FORCE — what the kindred is pursuing or struggling with now. Example: "Now thirty-two years post-Embrace, balancing forensic consultation for Lytton's court Sheriff against the original mortal commitment to honest documentation that the Embrace has not extinguished."

4. COTERIE ROLE — what the kindred provides to the coterie. Example: "The coterie's investigation specialist; the one who can read a crime scene's full story, including the kindred-involvement signs others miss."

CONCEPT TESTS:

A concept passes the kit's tests if:

- IT FITS THE CHRONICLE FRAME. A Camarilla orthodox Melbourne forensic-pathologist Tremere fits Lytton's court. A methuselah-tempo Sydney aesthetic-irrelevant accountant fits Sarrasine's audience less well.
- IT PRODUCES SCENES. The concept generates situations: court appearances, mortal-network maintenance, Discipline use under specific pressure, Touchstone engagement at recognisable stakes.
- IT HOLDS TENSION. The character is not at peace with their existence. The Tenets and Convictions push against each other; the Embrace has not resolved the mortal self entirely.
- IT'S DISTINCT FROM THE COTERIE. Coterie members with overlapping concepts struggle to differentiate in play. Each PC's concept should be readable as distinct in one sentence.

CONCEPT CATEGORIES (NOT EXCLUSIVE):

The kit recognises common V5 concept families. Each suits different chronicle modes:

- INVESTIGATOR / SCHOLAR — forensic specialist, occult researcher, historian, journalist. Suits Camarilla orthodox, Hecata family, cross-supernatural diplomatic.
- ENFORCER / SOLDIER — former military, police, security, criminal enforcer. Suits Brisbane Sabbat-survivor, Camarilla orthodox Sheriff-adjacent, Anarch Movement.
- POLITICIAN / SOCIALITE — connected social operator, former diplomat, political operative, network-rich figure. Suits Camarilla orthodox, methuselah-tempo Sydney audience-track.
- ARTIST / PERFORMER — visual artist, musician, performer, writer. Suits methuselah-tempo Sydney (Toreador-tradition primary), Camarilla orthodox Toreador track.
- CRAFTSPERSON / SPECIALIST — surgeon, engineer, mechanic, skilled trade specialist. Suits Brisbane Sabbat-survivor cells, Anarch Movement, Hecata family business-network.
- WANDERER / OUTSIDER — itinerant, refugee, displaced person, recent arrival. Suits Anarch Movement, cross-Pacific refusenik correspondence.
- INHERITOR / FAMILY-TRADITION — family-business successor, religious-tradition figure, dynastic position. Suits Hecata family primarily, Camarilla orthodox Ventrue track.
- CRIMINAL / OPERATOR — organised crime, smuggler, fence, fixer. Suits Brisbane Sabbat-survivor cells, Anarch Movement, certain Camarilla orthodox tracks.

MORTAL PAST DEPTH:

Kit-standard practice: write 1-3 paragraphs of mortal-past detail at character creation. Not full life history; specific anchor scenes:

- ONE FORMATIVE CHILDHOOD OR YOUNG-ADULT MOMENT that shaped the character's Convictions
- THE LAST MORTAL DAY before the events leading to Embrace
- AT LEAST ONE NAMED MORTAL FROM PRE-EMBRACE LIFE who may now be a Touchstone, a memory-anchor, or chronicle-active connection

The depth matters because Touchstones (Entry 9) often draw from mortal-past relationships. Thin mortal-past produces thin Touchstones.

EMBRACE CIRCUMSTANCE DEPTH:

Kit-standard practice: 1 paragraph of Embrace-specific detail:

- WHO embraced the character (sire identity at chronicle-relevant detail; full sire detail in Entry 12)
- WHEN (year, location, surrounding mortal circumstances)
- WHY (sire's reason; character's reason if consensual, or the absence of reason if not)
- IMMEDIATE AFTERMATH (first days post-Embrace; who taught the character about being kindred; how the character first fed)

Embrace circumstance often produces chronicle-active complications: a sire who is still chronicle-active, a Tenet violation in the Embrace itself, a Touchstone who witnessed or learned of the Embrace.

CURRENT DRIVING FORCE:

Kit-standard practice: 1-2 sentences capturing what the character is pursuing or struggling with NOW. Connects to Ambition (longer-arc goal) and Desires (session-scale wants).

The driving force should be:
- ACTIVE (the character is pursuing something, not waiting)
- COSTLY (pursuit produces Tenets-pressure, Convictions-pressure, Touchstone-pressure)
- ACHIEVABLE-OR-FAILABLE in chronicle scope ("learn to control my Beast over centuries" is not chronicle-active; "earn Status 3 in Lytton's court before October 2026" is)

COTERIE ROLE:

Kit-standard practice: 1 sentence describing what the character provides to the coterie:

- INVESTIGATION / INFORMATION ROLE — "I find what others miss"
- COMBAT / PROTECTION ROLE — "I am the coterie's defence"
- SOCIAL / DIPLOMACY ROLE — "I negotiate with court and rival kindred"
- TECHNICAL / SPECIALTY ROLE — "I handle the technical / occult / medical / financial work the coterie depends on"
- HEART / ETHICAL ROLE — "I keep the coterie connected to its Touchstones and Tenets"
- WILDCARD / CHAOS ROLE — "I produce the unpredictable element the coterie occasionally needs"

Coteries benefit from role-distribution; four investigators with no combat role struggle when combat occurs.

KIT NOTES:

- Camarilla orthodox concepts often emphasise mortal-past social-network depth (former politician, journalist, lawyer, academic) producing chronicle-active mortal-network operations.
- Brisbane Sabbat-survivor concepts often emphasise cell-utility (combat capability, technical specialty, ritual support) with mortal-past detail compressed (cells maintain operational secrecy at expense of mortal-past visibility).
- Methuselah-tempo Sydney concepts often emphasise aesthetic / cultural / performance capability that Sarrasine reads as competent; junior-kindred bureaucratic-or-administrative concepts feel diminished in this chronicle.
- Anarch Movement Footscray Crew concepts often emphasise multicultural-community embedding (specific cultural-cultivation depth, mortal-network density in named community) that produces chronicle-active neighbourhood operations.
- Hecata family Calabria Branch concepts often emphasise family-tradition-positioned mortal past (Italian-Australian family connection, Catholic-tradition embedding, business-network mortal-tier).
- Cross-supernatural diplomatic Cress Truce concepts often emphasise cross-splat-aware mortal past (urban planning, public-safety, journalism investigating supernatural-adjacent material) or kindred-with-Garou-respectful sire-tradition.

CLAN SELECTION

Clan defines the kindred's blood lineage — their Bane (hereditary curse), Compulsion (Bane-driven behavioural compulsion), in-clan Disciplines, and sect-political baseline. The kit supports all V5 clans plus Caitiff (clanless) and Thin-Blood.

For each clan: Bane summary, Compulsion summary, in-clan Disciplines, sect baseline, kit-chronicle suitability.

=== CAMARILLA-BASELINE CLANS ===

BRUJAH — "The Rabble"
- Bane: Bane of the Rebellious — when frenzying, Brujah suffer additional Difficulty on Composure rolls to resist Fury Frenzy; one less die on Composure resistance per Bane Severity.
- Compulsion: Rebellion — driven to oppose, disrupt, or undermine an authority or accepted position.
- In-clan Disciplines: Celerity, Potence, Presence.
- Sect baseline: historically Camarilla; significant Brujah presence in Anarch Movement since the Brujah-led Anarch revolt.
- Kit suitability: excellent for Anarch Movement Footscray Crew / Pilsen; strong for Camarilla orthodox enforcers and Sheriff-adjacent; viable for Brisbane Sabbat-survivor combat specialists; weak for methuselah-tempo Sydney (rebellion compulsion clashes with Sarrasine's register).

MALKAVIAN — "The Lunatics"
- Bane: Fractured Perspective — Malkavians suffer from Bane-tied mental aberration; one less die on Composure or Wits rolls when Bane Severity applies, reflecting fractured cognition.
- Compulsion: Delusion — driven to act on irrational perception, hallucination, or compulsive ritual.
- In-clan Disciplines: Auspex, Dominate, Obfuscate.
- Sect baseline: historically Camarilla; significant Sabbat-orthodox-tradition presence too.
- Kit suitability: strong for Camarilla orthodox (court Malkavians provide intelligence-gathering); strong for cross-supernatural diplomatic (Auspex-mediated perception suits Cress Truce framework intelligence work); viable for all chronicle modes with Bane-handling care (the Bane benefits from explicit table-discussion regarding mental-illness depiction).

NOSFERATU — "The Sewer Rats"
- Bane: Repulsiveness — Nosferatu are inhumanly disfigured; one less die on Social rolls involving appearance, and Bane increases Difficulty for blending in.
- Compulsion: Cryptophilia — driven to gather, hoard, and use secrets; cannot reveal a secret without compensation.
- In-clan Disciplines: Animalism, Obfuscate, Potence.
- Sect baseline: historically Camarilla; significant Anarch and independent presence.
- Kit suitability: excellent for information-specialist coteries in all modes; strong for Brisbane Sabbat-survivor cell intelligence; strong for cross-supernatural diplomatic information-gathering; Camarilla orthodox Melbourne maintains active Nosferatu informant network reporting to Sheriff.

TOREADOR — "The Degenerates"
- Bane: Aesthetic Fixation — when encountering beauty or artistic excellence, Toreador must succeed on Composure roll or be entranced; one less die on relevant rolls until they engage with the aesthetic.
- Compulsion: Obsession — driven to pursue an aesthetic, person, or experience to the exclusion of other priorities.
- In-clan Disciplines: Auspex, Celerity, Presence.
- Sect baseline: historically Camarilla; significant Anarch and independent presence; methuselah-tempo Sydney's Sarrasine is Toreador.
- Kit suitability: excellent for methuselah-tempo Sydney (Toreador-tradition primary clan; Sarrasine's audience favours Toreador-tradition aesthetic engagement); strong for Camarilla orthodox Melbourne (Lytton's court Toreador track is active); strong for Anarch Movement artist-track; viable for all modes.

TREMERE — "The Warlocks"
- Bane: Deficient Blood — Tremere blood cannot create bonds outside their own clan-tradition pyramid; one less die when attempting Blood Bond on non-Tremere targets.
- Compulsion: Perfectionism — driven to redo, refine, or perfect any incomplete task; the Beast pushes them to obsessive task-completion.
- In-clan Disciplines: Auspex, Dominate, Blood Sorcery (the clan's signature ritual Discipline).
- Sect baseline: Camarilla; the Tremere pyramid is significantly weakened post-V5-canon Tremere Schism but operates within Camarilla orthodox.
- Kit suitability: excellent for Camarilla orthodox courts (court Tremere is standard position; Blood Sorcery rituals are operational chronicle resource); strong for cross-supernatural diplomatic (Tremere Auspex-tradition + Blood Sorcery rituals support framework operations); viable for other modes with sect-political handling; the kit's Melbourne court Tremere is named NPC; PCs may be apprentices or junior pyramid members.

VENTRUE — "The Blue Bloods"
- Bane: Rarefied Tastes — Ventrue may only feed from specific vessel-types (the player defines the preference at character creation: a specific blood-type, gender, profession, ethnicity, etc.); feeding from outside preference produces immediate Aggravated damage or rejection.
- Compulsion: Arrogance — driven to assert authority, demand precedence, or impose will on others.
- In-clan Disciplines: Dominate, Fortitude, Presence.
- Sect baseline: Camarilla orthodox primary; Ventrue defines Camarilla orthodox tradition in many domains; Lytton (Melbourne) and Octavia Marsh (Adelaide) are both Ventrue 7th-gen Princes.
- Kit suitability: excellent for Camarilla orthodox (Ventrue track is institutional-power baseline; Princes Lytton and Octavia Marsh are Ventrue); strong for political-pursuit Ambitions in any mode; weak for Anarch Movement (Ventrue Arrogance Compulsion clashes with Movement Tenets); viable for methuselah-tempo Sydney (Ventrue at Sarrasine's audience operate at her register, not their own).

=== INDEPENDENT / CROSS-SECT CLANS ===

BANU HAQIM — "The Assassins" (formerly Children of Haqim)
- Bane: Blood Addiction — when Banu Haqim taste kindred Vitae, they must succeed on Hunger Frenzy resistance or attempt to drain the source; Bane Severity increases Difficulty.
- Compulsion: Judgement — driven to apply judgment-tradition to perceived transgression; the Beast pushes them to enact the family-tradition judicial role.
- In-clan Disciplines: Blood Sorcery, Celerity, Obfuscate.
- Sect baseline: historically Sabbat-aligned via specific tradition lines; significant Camarilla orthodox presence post-V5 reconciliation; Brisbane Sabbat-survivor includes a Banu Haqim sorcerer-in-residence supporting cell ritual work.
- Kit suitability: excellent for Brisbane Sabbat-survivor (cell-tradition sorcery support); strong for Camarilla orthodox Sheriff-adjacent operations; viable for cross-supernatural diplomatic (Blood Sorcery rituals support framework operations); the kit's Brisbane Banu Haqim sorcerer-in-residence is mentor-tier NPC for PC Banu Haqim apprentices.

GANGREL — "The Outlanders"
- Bane: Bestial Features — when frenzying or when Bane Severity applies, Gangrel manifest animal features (claws, fur, fangs, eyes); one less die on Social rolls when features are visible.
- Compulsion: Feral Impulses — driven to abandon human conventions and act on animal instinct; the Beast pushes them toward primal action.
- In-clan Disciplines: Animalism, Fortitude, Protean.
- Sect baseline: traditionally independent / Anarch; Gangrel are notoriously sect-skeptical and often operate outside formal sect structure; some Camarilla orthodox courts maintain Gangrel as Sheriffs or scouts.
- Kit suitability: strong for Anarch Movement (Movement-tradition Gangrel are common); strong for Brisbane Sabbat-survivor scouts and wilderness-operations; viable for cross-supernatural diplomatic (Gangrel Animalism supports Garou-tradition communication); weak for methuselah-tempo Sydney (Sarrasine's aesthetic-tradition treats feral-manifestation as graceless).

LASOMBRA — "The Keepers"
- Bane: Distorted Image — Lasombra cast no reflection and produce distorted images in modern recording devices (photos, video, digital); one less die on Stealth-failures and Masquerade-related rolls involving documentation.
- Compulsion: Ruthlessness — driven to seize advantage at any cost; the Beast pushes them toward predatory exploitation.
- In-clan Disciplines: Dominate, Oblivion, Potence.
- Sect baseline: traditionally Sabbat-orthodoxy primary; significant refusenik presence (Cardinal Reyna in Pacific Northwest is Lasombra-refusenik); some Camarilla orthodox post-V5 reconciliation Lasombra exist; Templar Constance Abernathy (Brisbane Sabbat-survivor) is Lasombra antitribu.
- Kit suitability: excellent for Brisbane Sabbat-survivor cells; strong for cross-Pacific refusenik chronicles (Pacific Northwest Cardinal Reyna's domain); viable for Camarilla orthodox with reconciliation-tradition handling; the Brisbane Templar Constance Abernathy provides Lasombra mentor-tier NPC.

MINISTRY — "The Serpents" (formerly Followers of Set)
- Bane: Cold-Blooded — Ministry are physically averse to bright light; suffer additional Difficulty in sun-bright environments and one less die on rolls involving Sun-presence even in sheltered environments.
- Compulsion: Transgression — driven to lead others into ethical violation, sin, or compromised behaviour; the Beast pushes them to corrupting influence.
- In-clan Disciplines: Obfuscate, Presence, Protean.
- Sect baseline: historically Independent; significant Anarch presence; some Camarilla orthodox post-V5 Ministry presence; Sabbat-tradition Ministry less common.
- Kit suitability: strong for Anarch Movement (transgression-tradition fits Movement boundary-defiance); viable for Camarilla orthodox with corruption-tradition handling; viable for cross-supernatural diplomatic (Ministry Obfuscate supports framework intelligence); weak for Brisbane Sabbat-survivor (cell-tradition cohesion resists transgression-tradition Compulsion).

RAVNOS — "The Daredevils"
- Bane: Doomed — Ravnos who remain in the same place for more than two nights face the Bane's effect: spontaneous fire damage; one Aggravated damage per night beyond the second, escalating until they relocate.
- Compulsion: Tempting Fate — driven to take a high-risk action when opportunity presents; the Beast pushes them toward gambles.
- In-clan Disciplines: Animalism, Obfuscate, Presence.
- Sect baseline: historically Independent; significant Anarch presence; post-V5 Ravnos remnant population is small (clan was significantly reduced in late-twentieth-century events documented in kit reference material).
- Kit suitability: strong for itinerant / cross-Pacific correspondence concepts; viable for Anarch Movement; weak for Camarilla orthodox (Doomed Bane prevents domain-stability); weak for Brisbane Sabbat-survivor (cell-stability requirement clashes with Doomed Bane); viable for cross-supernatural diplomatic correspondence specialists.

THE HECATA — "The Necromancers" (family-tradition merger of Cappadocian / Giovanni / Samedi / Harbingers of Skulls tradition lines)
- Bane: Painful Kiss — Hecata feeding produces pain in the vessel rather than ecstasy; vessels suffer one die penalty on resisting rolls but actively resist feeding more than non-Hecata feeding.
- Compulsion: Morbidity — driven to engage with death, mortality, decay, or wraith-tradition material; the Beast pushes them toward death-fixation.
- In-clan Disciplines: Auspex, Fortitude, Oblivion.
- Sect baseline: Hecata operates as sect-of-clans rather than within Camarilla / Sabbat / Anarch sect structure; family-tradition primacy; the kit's Calabria Branch (Melbourne) and Bridgeport Six (Chicago) are Hecata family branches.
- Kit suitability: REQUIRED for Hecata family chronicles (Calabria Branch, Bridgeport Six); viable as cross-sect ally in Camarilla orthodox or Anarch Movement chronicles with family-tradition handling; the Hecata family-tradition prohibits diablerie within family lineages (kit Tenet-level).

SALUBRI — "The Healers" (formerly Soul-Eaters)
- Bane: Hunted — Salubri Vitae is sought by other kindred (a legacy of pre-V5 events); when other kindred taste Salubri Vitae they receive significant Hunger reduction, producing chronicle-active threat. Bane mechanic: Salubri identifiable to specific Auspex and Dominate effects, increasing detection.
- Compulsion: Affective Empathy — driven to assist suffering creatures (mortal or kindred); the Beast pushes them toward intervention regardless of cost.
- In-clan Disciplines: Auspex, Dominate, Fortitude.
- Sect baseline: rare; small remnant population; sect-political position uncertain; significant Anarch Movement and Independent presence; some Camarilla orthodox post-V5 Salubri reconciliation.
- Kit suitability: viable for any chronicle mode with Hunted Bane handling care; strong for cross-supernatural diplomatic (Affective Empathy Compulsion supports framework cooperation); strong for Anarch Movement (Salubri tradition aligns with Movement Touchstone-tradition); the kit treats Salubri as rare and chronicle-shaping when present.

TZIMISCE — "The Old Clan" (formerly Fiends)
- Bane: Grounded — Tzimisce must sleep with at least two handfuls of native soil within proximity of their resting place; failure to do so produces one less die on all rolls and accelerated Hunger production.
- Compulsion: Covetousness — driven to claim, possess, or control specific objects, places, or people; the Beast pushes them toward acquisitive fixation.
- In-clan Disciplines: Animalism, Dominate, Protean (with Vicissitude-tradition flesh-shaping accessible via clan-specific Protean rituals and Storyteller approval).
- Sect baseline: historically Sabbat-orthodox primary; significant refusenik presence (Cardinal Magdalena in Russian Far East is Tzimisce-tradition refusenik); Bishop Callista Vox (Brisbane Sabbat-survivor) is Tzimisce 7th-gen.
- Kit suitability: excellent for Brisbane Sabbat-survivor (Bishop Callista Vox preservation aesthetic is Tzimisce flesh-craft tradition); strong for cross-Pacific refusenik (Cardinal Magdalena's domain); viable for Anarch Movement Tzimisce-tradition; weak for Camarilla orthodox (clan tradition is Sabbat-deep and reconciliation rare); the Brisbane Bishop provides Tzimisce mentor-tier NPC for PC Tzimisce within Brisbane Sabbat-survivor chronicles.

=== CLANLESS AND PROTO-CLAN ===

CAITIFF — "The Clanless"
- Bane: Outcast — Caitiff are clanless; suffer one less die on Social rolls in clan-tradition formal contexts (Camarilla orthodox courts, Sabbat ritus, Hecata family-tradition gatherings); also lack clan-tradition mentor / training infrastructure.
- Compulsion: none specific; Caitiff manifest variable Compulsions per Storyteller / player negotiation.
- In-clan Disciplines: any two Disciplines except Blood Sorcery and Oblivion (player choice with Storyteller approval); typically one of Animalism, Auspex, Celerity, Dominate, Fortitude, Obfuscate, Potence, Presence, Protean.
- Sect baseline: variable; Anarch Movement treats Caitiff with relative welcome; Camarilla orthodox treats Caitiff with suspicion and lower-status assignment; Sabbat-tradition treats Caitiff variably (some packs welcome; some reject).
- Kit suitability: strong for Anarch Movement (Caitiff are welcome in Movement); viable for Camarilla orthodox with status-handling complications; viable for Brisbane Sabbat-survivor; the Caitiff status is itself chronicle-active material — finding sire, gaining clan recognition, or remaining proudly clanless are all valid Ambitions.

THIN-BLOOD — "The Duskborn"
- Bane: Thin-Blooded — Thin-Blood are weakly Embraced (high-generation, often 14th-16th); cannot create ghouls reliably, blood bonds are unstable, some daywalking capability, Discipline access via Thin-Blood Alchemy only (cannot learn standard Disciplines).
- Compulsion: none in standard sense; Thin-Blood operate with variable Beast-pressure that differs from full Kindred experience.
- Disciplines: Thin-Blood Alchemy only (the Discipline-equivalent system specific to Thin-Blood); the Alchemy framework provides Thin-Blood-tier capabilities through ritual mixing of blood with reagents.
- Sect baseline: rejected by Camarilla orthodox and Sabbat-orthodoxy; accepted by Anarch Movement with full status; Hecata family-tradition variable acceptance.
- Kit suitability: strong for Anarch Movement Footscray Crew / Pilsen (Movement-tradition Thin-Blood inclusion is doctrinal); viable for chronicle modes with Thin-Blood-handling care; weak for Camarilla orthodox or methuselah-tempo Sydney (status-tradition rejects Thin-Blood); the Thin-Blood status produces chronicle-active sect-political pressure as Tenet-level material.

CLAN-SELECTION QUESTIONS:

- Does the clan fit the chronicle mode and city? See per-clan suitability above.
- Does the Bane produce chronicle-active situations the player wants to engage? Ventrue feeding restriction, Ravnos travel compulsion, Nosferatu appearance disability, Hecata painful kiss all produce specific scene-types.
- Does the Compulsion produce play opportunities the player wants? Brujah Rebellion, Toreador Obsession, Tremere Perfectionism, Lasombra Ruthlessness produce different scene-driving patterns.
- Are in-clan Disciplines aligned with the character's role and coterie need? See Entry 6 for starting Discipline selection.
- Is the clan's sect-political position compatible with the coterie and chronicle? An Anarch Movement coterie with three Ventrue PCs produces internal tension; a Camarilla orthodox coterie with a Tzimisce PC produces external tension.

KIT NOTES:

- Camarilla orthodox Melbourne distribution: Ventrue, Toreador, Tremere, Malkavian, Nosferatu, Brujah common; Banu Haqim, Lasombra (reconciled), Gangrel possible; others requiring Storyteller-approval handling.
- Brisbane Sabbat-survivor distribution: Tzimisce, Lasombra (antitribu), Banu Haqim common; Brujah (survivor-tradition), Gangrel, Malkavian possible; Camarilla-baseline clans rare and chronicle-active when present.
- Methuselah-tempo Sydney distribution: Toreador (primary), Tremere, Ventrue, Malkavian, Lasombra (Sarrasine-permitted) common; other clans at Sarrasine's discretion.
- Anarch Movement Footscray Crew distribution: Brujah, Gangrel, Caitiff, Thin-Blood common; Nosferatu, Malkavian, Ministry, Toreador possible; Ventrue rare and ideologically complicated.
- Hecata family Calabria Branch distribution: Hecata (required for family branch position); Hecata-tradition allied clans (rare and chronicle-specific) possible.
- Cross-supernatural diplomatic Cress Truce distribution: any clan; Malkavian, Tremere, Auspex-heavy clans favoured for intelligence work; Gangrel favoured for Garou-tradition communication; clans with cross-splat-relevant capabilities favoured.

ATTRIBUTES

Nine Attributes distributed across three categories (Physical, Social, Mental) via priority distribution (Entry 1: Primary 4/3/2, Secondary 3/3/2, Tertiary 3/2/2 with all Attributes starting at 1).

PHYSICAL ATTRIBUTES:

STRENGTH — raw physical power, capacity for damage in close combat, lifting / breaking / forcing.
- 1: weak (a frail elder mortal)
- 2: typical mortal adult
- 3: athletic mortal
- 4: trained athlete or kindred-enhanced
- 5: peak kindred-physical (Brujah or Gangrel with Potence-enhanced baseline)
- Used for: Brawl damage, Melee damage, Athletics (lifting / forcing), grappling, breaking objects

DEXTERITY — speed, agility, fine motor control, reflex.
- 1: clumsy
- 2: typical mortal
- 3: nimble
- 4: kindred-tier reflex
- 5: peak kindred-agile (Celerity-enhanced baseline)
- Used for: Athletics (acrobatics), Brawl (dodge), Firearms, Larceny, Stealth, Drive, defence rolls

STAMINA — physical resilience, endurance, capacity to absorb damage.
- 1: frail
- 2: typical mortal
- 3: hardy
- 4: kindred-resilient
- 5: peak kindred-durable (Fortitude-enhanced baseline)
- Used for: Health derivation (Stamina + 3), Athletics (endurance), Survival (resisting environmental damage), resistance rolls

SOCIAL ATTRIBUTES:

CHARISMA — magnetism, likability, force of personality.
- 1: off-putting
- 2: typical
- 3: warm or compelling
- 4: magnetic
- 5: legendary (Presence-tier baseline)
- Used for: Persuasion, Performance, Leadership, Animal Ken (handling), Intimidation (presence-based)

MANIPULATION — capacity for deception, persuasion-by-pressure, social maneuvering.
- 1: transparent
- 2: typical
- 3: capable manipulator
- 4: skilled deceiver
- 5: peerless
- Used for: Subterfuge, Persuasion (deception-based), Intimidation (threat-based), Insight (against), Streetwise

COMPOSURE — emotional self-control, poise, resistance to social pressure and Frenzy.
- 1: volatile
- 2: typical
- 3: poised
- 4: imperturbable
- 5: methuselah-tempo poise
- Used for: Willpower derivation (Composure + Resolve), Insight, resistance to Intimidation and emotional manipulation, Frenzy resistance, Awareness (calm observation)

MENTAL ATTRIBUTES:

INTELLIGENCE — reasoning, knowledge retention, capacity for analysis.
- 1: limited cognition
- 2: typical
- 3: bright
- 4: scholarly
- 5: peerless intellect
- Used for: Academics, Science, Investigation (analytical), Occult (knowledge-based), Technology, Medicine

WITS — perception, reaction speed, quick thinking under pressure.
- 1: slow to perceive
- 2: typical
- 3: sharp
- 4: quick-thinking
- 5: peerless perception
- Used for: Awareness, Investigation (observation), Larceny (under pressure), Stealth (reactive), Survival (reading environment), defence rolls

RESOLVE — focus, determination, capacity to persist under pressure.
- 1: easily distracted
- 2: typical
- 3: focused
- 4: relentless
- 5: legendary will
- Used for: Willpower derivation (Composure + Resolve), Investigation (sustained), Occult (ritual focus), Medicine (sustained operation), resistance to Discipline coercion and mental influence

ATTRIBUTE SELECTION GUIDANCE:

Match Attributes to character role:

- COMBAT-FOCUSED PC: Physical Primary (Strength 3, Dexterity 4, Stamina 2 standard; or Dexterity 3, Strength 4, Stamina 2 for Brawl-heavy)
- SOCIAL-OPERATOR PC: Social Primary (Charisma 4, Composure 3, Manipulation 2; or Manipulation 4, Charisma 2, Composure 3)
- INVESTIGATOR / SCHOLAR PC: Mental Primary (Intelligence 4, Wits 3, Resolve 2; or Wits 4, Intelligence 3, Resolve 2)
- HYBRID PC: Secondary balances; Tertiary covers gap

NO ATTRIBUTE BELOW 1: each starts at 1 minimum.

NO ATTRIBUTE ABOVE 4 AT CREATION: starting Attributes cap at 4 (5 requires Discipline-enhancement or chronicle-progression).

KIT NOTES:

- Camarilla orthodox courts reward Composure (formal interaction) and Manipulation (status politics); Resolve supports Disciplines resistance.
- Brisbane Sabbat-survivor cells reward Stamina (resilience), Dexterity (tactical operations), Resolve (Disciplines resistance and ritual support).
- Methuselah-tempo Sydney audiences reward Composure (poise at Sarrasine's register), Charisma (aesthetic presence), Resolve (methuselah-tempo extended-scene endurance).
- Anarch Movement neighbourhoods reward Charisma (mortal-network maintenance), Wits (street-level reactive perception), Manipulation (operating against Camarilla orthodox pressure).
- Hecata family branches reward Intelligence (necromantic-tradition scholarship), Composure (family-tradition formal interaction), Resolve (ritual focus).
- Cross-supernatural diplomatic Cress Truce work rewards Composure (cross-splat poise), Intelligence (treaty-protocol mastery), Wits (cross-splat reactive reading).

SKILLS AND SPECIALTIES

27 Skills distributed via three priority options (Jack-of-All-Trades, Balanced, Specialist; see Entry 1). Skills group into Physical, Social, Mental.

PHYSICAL SKILLS:

ATHLETICS — running, climbing, swimming, jumping, throwing, lifting. Used with Strength for power moves, Dexterity for acrobatics, Stamina for endurance.

BRAWL — unarmed combat, grappling, biting. Used with Strength for damage, Dexterity for defence.

CRAFT — making, repairing, modifying physical objects. Specialty required if rated. Example specialties: Carpentry, Metalwork, Vehicle Repair, Jewellery, Tailoring, Bookbinding.

DRIVE — operating motor vehicles. Cars, trucks, motorcycles. Specialty for unusual vehicles (Heavy Goods, Motorcycles, Boats, Light Aircraft).

FIREARMS — operating ranged weapons. Pistols, rifles, shotguns, submachine guns. Common specialty: Pistols, Rifles, Shotguns, Tactical (military / police firearm doctrine).

LARCENY — lockpicking, pickpocketing, breaking-and-entering, sleight of hand. Specialty: Lockpicking, Pickpocketing, Security Systems, Safe-cracking.

MELEE — armed close combat. Knives, swords, clubs, improvised weapons. Specialty: Knives, Swords, Improvised, Polearms.

STEALTH — moving unseen, hiding, evading detection. Specialty: Urban, Wilderness, Crowd-blending, Shadowing.

SURVIVAL — wilderness operation, environmental adaptation, tracking, finding shelter. Specialty: Urban Survival, Wilderness, Coastal, Desert, Arctic.

SOCIAL SKILLS:

ANIMAL KEN — handling and understanding animals. Specialty: Dogs, Horses, Birds of Prey, Pack Animals.

ETIQUETTE — formal social interaction, cultural protocols. Specialty: Camarilla Elysium, Sabbat Ritus, Diplomatic Corps, Corporate Boardroom, Cross-Cultural.

INSIGHT — reading others, detecting deception, understanding motivation. Specialty: Detecting Lies, Empathy, Emotional Intelligence, Reading Kindred.

INTIMIDATION — coercing through threat or presence. Specialty: Physical Threats, Stare-down, Implied Violence, Verbal Coercion.

LEADERSHIP — organising and directing others. Specialty: Military Command, Inspirational, Cell Leadership, Court Politics.

PERFORMANCE — artistic performance for audience. Specialty required if rated. Example: Violin, Vocal, Dance, Acting, Stand-Up, Public Speaking.

PERSUASION — convincing through reason or emotional appeal. Specialty: Negotiation, Seduction, Inspiration, Bargaining.

STREETWISE — navigating urban underclass and criminal subculture. Specialty: Drug Trade, Black Market, Gangs, Sex Work, Smuggling, Specific City (Melbourne / Brisbane / Sydney etc).

SUBTERFUGE — deception, disguise, social manipulation through indirect means. Specialty: Long Cons, Lying, Disguise, Misdirection.

MENTAL SKILLS:

ACADEMICS — formal scholarship, history, literature, language. Specialty required if rated. Example: Medieval History, Literature, Classical Languages, Religion, Philosophy, Specific Period (Edwardian, Victorian, Twentieth Century).

AWARENESS — perceiving environment, noticing details, situational alertness. Specialty: Crowds, Wilderness, Combat, Supernatural Cues, Specific Domain.

FINANCE — money, banking, investment, economic systems. Specialty: Money Laundering, Stock Market, Mortal-Network Funding, Cryptocurrency, Black-Market Economics.

INVESTIGATION — research, evidence-gathering, deduction. Specialty: Forensic Pathology, Crime Scenes, Documentary Research, Surveillance, Specific Subject Matter.

MEDICINE — diagnosis, treatment, surgery, pharmacology. Specialty: Surgery, Forensic Medicine, Veterinary, Trauma, Pharmacology, Specific Specialty (Cardiology, Neurology, etc.).

OCCULT — supernatural knowledge, magical theory, lore. Specialty: Vampire Lore, Werewolf Lore, Garou Lore, Ritual Magic, Specific Tradition (Hecata Family-Tradition, Tremere Lore, Cross-Pacific Refusenik Tradition).

POLITICS — political systems, institutional operation, sect politics. Specialty: Camarilla, Anarch Movement, Sabbat-Survivor, Cross-Pacific Refusenik, Local Mortal (Victorian State, Queensland State, Federal Australian), Cross-Splat (Cress Truce Framework).

SCIENCE — scientific knowledge, experimental method, technical theory. Specialty required if rated. Example: Chemistry, Biology, Physics, Engineering, Computer Science, Forensic Science.

TECHNOLOGY — computing, electronics, modern technical systems. Specialty: Programming, Hacking, Network Security, Hardware, Specific Platform (Linux, Mobile, Embedded Systems).

SPECIALTIES PROCEDURE:

Three Specialties at character creation:

1. MANDATORY SPECIALTY: if PC has dots in Academics, Craft, Performance, or Science, one Specialty must be in one of these Skills.
2. TWO ADDITIONAL SPECIALTIES: player-chosen on any rated Skill.

Effect: +1 die when the Specialty applies to a roll.

SPECIALTY GUIDANCE:

- Choose Specialties matching character role and chronicle context. "Investigation (Forensic Pathology)" suits a Melbourne forensic-pathologist PC; "Streetwise (Brisbane Industrial Zones)" suits a Brisbane Sabbat-survivor cell operative.
- Specialties may be chronicle-specific or character-specific. Both produce mechanical bonus; chronicle-specific Specialties also provide narrative anchor.
- Avoid over-specialised Specialties that rarely apply. "Persuasion (Negotiating with Mexican-American Anarch Movement Activists)" applies rarely; "Persuasion (Negotiation)" applies broadly.

SKILL DISTRIBUTION GUIDANCE:

- JACK-OF-ALL-TRADES (1×3, 8×2, 10×1) suits broad-capability PCs without deep specialty. Suits Anarch Movement Footscray Crew breadth-required operatives.
- BALANCED (1×3, 3×2, 7×1) suits mid-range PCs with moderate specialisation. Suits Camarilla orthodox status-pursuit PCs, cross-supernatural diplomatic PCs.
- SPECIALIST (1×4, 3×3, 3×2, 3×1) suits deep-specialty PCs. Suits Brisbane Sabbat-survivor cell specialists, methuselah-tempo Sydney aesthetic specialists, Hecata family family-tradition specialists.

KIT NOTES:

- Camarilla orthodox skill priorities: Etiquette, Politics (Camarilla), Persuasion, Insight, Investigation, Awareness, Subterfuge, Academics (relevant history).
- Brisbane Sabbat-survivor cell priorities: Stealth, Brawl, Firearms, Streetwise, Occult (relevant tradition), Investigation, Survival (Urban), Technology.
- Methuselah-tempo Sydney priorities: Etiquette, Performance, Persuasion, Insight, Academics, Occult, Awareness, Subterfuge.
- Anarch Movement Footscray Crew priorities: Streetwise, Persuasion, Brawl or Firearms, Drive, Larceny, Subterfuge, Politics (Movement), specific Cultural Specialties.
- Hecata family Calabria Branch priorities: Occult (Hecata family-tradition), Academics (necromantic / family history), Investigation, Finance, Politics (family-tradition), Insight, Medicine.
- Cross-supernatural diplomatic Cress Truce priorities: Etiquette, Politics (Cress Truce), Occult (Werewolf Lore), Insight, Awareness, Investigation, Persuasion, Technology.

STARTING DISCIPLINES

At character creation, the PC receives:

- TWO DOTS IN IN-CLAN DISCIPLINES (one Discipline at rating 2, OR two Disciplines at rating 1 each)
- ONE ADDITIONAL DOT FROM PREDATOR TYPE (Entry 7), which may extend in-clan or grant access to specific out-of-clan Discipline per Predator Type

IN-CLAN DISCIPLINE LISTS (recap from Entry 3):

- Banu Haqim: Blood Sorcery, Celerity, Obfuscate
- Brujah: Celerity, Potence, Presence
- Gangrel: Animalism, Fortitude, Protean
- Hecata: Auspex, Fortitude, Oblivion
- Lasombra: Dominate, Oblivion, Potence
- Malkavian: Auspex, Dominate, Obfuscate
- Ministry: Obfuscate, Presence, Protean
- Nosferatu: Animalism, Obfuscate, Potence
- Ravnos: Animalism, Obfuscate, Presence
- Salubri: Auspex, Dominate, Fortitude
- Toreador: Auspex, Celerity, Presence
- Tremere: Auspex, Dominate, Blood Sorcery
- Tzimisce: Animalism, Dominate, Protean (with Vicissitude tradition)
- Ventrue: Dominate, Fortitude, Presence

Clanless / Proto-clan:
- Caitiff: any two Disciplines except Blood Sorcery and Oblivion (player choice with Storyteller approval)
- Thin-Blood: Thin-Blood Alchemy only

DISCIPLINE OVERVIEW (full mechanics in vtm_v5_disciplines_detailed.json):

ANIMALISM — communicate with, command, and bond with animals. Strong for tracking, scouting, intimidation through animal proxies. Iconic clans: Gangrel, Nosferatu, Tzimisce, Ravnos, Hecata-adjacent.

AUSPEX — heightened senses, mental perception, premonition, sensing the supernatural. Strong for investigation, court intelligence, Garou-tradition perception. Iconic clans: Malkavian, Toreador, Tremere, Salubri, Hecata.

BLOOD SORCERY — ritual magic powered by Vitae. Strong for ritual support, defensive magic, divination. Requires Discipline rating dots + specific ritual learning. Iconic clans: Tremere (specialty), Banu Haqim (tradition).

CELERITY — supernatural speed, reaction time, agility. Strong for combat, evasion, time-critical tasks. Iconic clans: Brujah, Toreador, Banu Haqim.

DOMINATE — mental coercion, memory modification, behavioural compulsion. Strong for social-combat, Masquerade maintenance, interrogation. Iconic clans: Ventrue, Malkavian, Tremere, Tzimisce, Lasombra, Salubri.

FORTITUDE — supernatural resilience, damage resistance, soak. Strong for tank-role, surviving Aggravated damage, daysleeping resilience. Iconic clans: Gangrel, Ventrue, Hecata, Salubri.

OBFUSCATE — concealment, disguise, invisibility, identity obscuration. Strong for stealth, infiltration, Masquerade maintenance. Iconic clans: Nosferatu, Malkavian, Banu Haqim, Ravnos, Ministry.

OBLIVION — necromantic and shadow magic, communicating with the dead, manipulating shadow. Hecata and Lasombra each access different tradition lines. Strong for ritual work, intelligence-gathering via wraith-tradition, shadow-tier combat. Iconic clans: Hecata (necromantic tradition), Lasombra (shadow tradition).

POTENCE — supernatural strength, damage dealing, lifting / breaking. Strong for combat damage, intimidation. Iconic clans: Brujah, Lasombra, Nosferatu.

PRESENCE — supernatural charisma, emotional manipulation, awe, terror. Strong for social-combat, leadership, crowd control. Iconic clans: Toreador, Ventrue, Brujah, Ministry, Ravnos.

PROTEAN — physical transformation, claws, animal forms, earth-melding. Strong for combat, stealth, escape. Iconic clans: Gangrel, Tzimisce (with Vicissitude), Ministry.

THIN-BLOOD ALCHEMY — Thin-Blood-exclusive ritual mixing of blood with reagents to produce variable supernatural effects. Distinctive Discipline-equivalent system. Iconic to Thin-Blood; non-Thin-Blood Kindred cannot learn.

STARTING DISCIPLINE SELECTION GUIDANCE:

Match starting Disciplines to character role:

- COMBAT-FOCUSED PC: Celerity, Potence, or Fortitude (defensive) at 2 dots; OR one combat Discipline at 1 + Presence (for intimidation) at 1.
- INVESTIGATOR PC: Auspex 2 (premonition + heightened senses), OR Auspex 1 + Dominate 1 (interrogation support).
- SOCIAL OPERATOR PC: Presence 2 (Awe and Daunt at 2 dots), OR Presence 1 + Dominate 1 (mental + social pressure).
- STEALTH OPERATOR PC: Obfuscate 2 (Cloak of Shadows + Unseen Presence), OR Obfuscate 1 + Auspex 1 (counter-stealth perception).
- RITUAL SPECIALIST: Blood Sorcery 2 (for Tremere / Banu Haqim) or Oblivion 2 (for Hecata / Lasombra); ritual capabilities require separate ritual-learning at Storyteller approval (see vtm_v5_rituals_ceremonies.json).
- PROTEAN-CAPABLE PC: Protean 2 for Gangrel produces Earth-Meld + animal-form access; Protean 1 for Ministry / Tzimisce provides specialty access.

DISCIPLINE CONSIDERATIONS BY CHRONICLE MODE:

CAMARILLA ORTHODOX MELBOURNE:
- Dominate is operational currency (Sheriff and Prince use Dominate; PCs may train to resist or to use within sanctioned contexts)
- Auspex supports court intelligence work and is highly valued
- Presence supports court status pursuit
- Obfuscate supports Masquerade-maintenance work
- Blood Sorcery (Tremere PCs) supports court Tremere position

BRISBANE SABBAT-SURVIVOR:
- Vicissitude-tradition Protean (Tzimisce PCs) supports Bishop Callista Vox's preservation aesthetic
- Potence and Celerity support cell combat operations
- Obfuscate supports cell concealment and federal-investigation evasion
- Blood Sorcery (Banu Haqim sorcerer-in-residence mentors) supports cell ritual work
- Oblivion (Lasombra antitribu Templar Constance Abernathy mentors) supports shadow-tier operations

METHUSELAH-TEMPO SYDNEY:
- Auspex supports reading Sarrasine's audience register
- Presence supports aesthetic-engagement
- Celerity supports aesthetic-performance (artistic-physical disciplines)
- Dominate is Sarrasine's preserve; PC Dominate use in Sydney is observed

ANARCH MOVEMENT FOOTSCRAY CREW:
- Celerity supports neighbourhood mobility
- Potence supports neighbourhood-defence operations
- Presence supports mortal-network influence
- Animalism supports working-class kindred animal-connection traditions
- Obfuscate supports operating against Camarilla orthodox pressure

HECATA FAMILY CALABRIA BRANCH:
- Oblivion is family-tradition primary; wraith-tradition consultation requires Oblivion ritual support
- Auspex supports family-tradition intelligence work
- Fortitude supports family-tradition resilience

CROSS-SUPERNATURAL DIPLOMATIC CRESS TRUCE:
- Auspex supports cross-splat intelligence work
- Animalism supports Garou-tradition communication (Animalism reads Garou as animal-aspect; not full Garou communication but supportive)
- Dominate is restricted in joint zones (Cress Truce treaty prohibits coercive Discipline use against Garou in joint zones)
- Presence supports framework diplomacy

DISCIPLINE PROGRESSION:

Starting Disciplines are baseline; PCs gain additional dots through Experience expenditure across chronicle. In-clan Disciplines cost less Experience than out-of-clan. See vtm_v5_core_mechanics.json for Experience expenditure rules.

KIT NOTES:

- Discipline ratings at chronicle start cap at 2 (rating 3+ requires Experience expenditure or chronicle-progression).
- Ritual-tier Blood Sorcery and Oblivion access requires both Discipline rating AND specific ritual learning at Storyteller approval; chronicle-start PCs typically have 0-1 specific rituals.
- Predator Type Discipline dot is in addition to the two in-clan starting dots; this third dot may extend in-clan or grant Predator-Type-specific out-of-clan access.
- Caitiff Disciplines are chosen at character creation and persist; later additional Disciplines require Experience expenditure and Storyteller-approved Embrace-tradition or mentor-tradition justification.

7.content:
PREDATOR TYPES

Predator Type defines the PC's feeding methodology — how they hunt vessels, where they feed, what they leave behind. Selection occurs at character creation and provides:

- ONE SPECIALTY (in Predator-Type-specific Skill)
- ONE DISCIPLINE DOT (Predator-Type-specific Discipline, may be in-clan or out-of-clan)
- ADVANTAGES AND FLAWS (Predator-Type-specific)

Predator Type also shapes mortal-network relationship, Masquerade-pressure baseline, and ethical-register of feeding scenes (Stains accumulation patterns vary by methodology).

=== KIT-SUPPORTED PREDATOR TYPES ===

ALLEYCAT — opportunistic violent feeding from strangers in vulnerable circumstances. Hunting in alleys, parks, transit-corridors. Vessel rarely remembers clearly; sometimes left injured or dead.
- Specialty: Intimidation (Stickups) or Brawl (Grappling)
- Discipline: Celerity 1 or Potence 1
- Advantages: +1 Criminal Contact (mortal); Humanity adjustment varies
- Flaws: -1 Status with Camarilla orthodox (Masquerade pressure from violence pattern)
- Suits: Anarch Movement, Brisbane Sabbat-survivor cell-operative, certain Camarilla orthodox enforcer concepts
- Stains pattern: high frequency Stains from violent feeding

BAGGER — purchases or steals blood from blood banks, hospitals, or medical-network sources. Distant from vessels; clinical feeding.
- Specialty: Larceny (Hospital Theft) or Streetwise (Black Market)
- Discipline: Obfuscate 1 or Dominate 1
- Advantages: +1 Resources (modest) or +1 Contacts (medical network)
- Flaws: Iron Gullet (cannot feed directly from living vessels without significant effort); Enemy if blood-bank theft pattern discovered
- Suits: Camarilla orthodox medical-network concepts, Brisbane cell logistics, Hecata family medical-front operations
- Stains pattern: low Stains from direct feeding; chronicle-active Masquerade pressure from acquisition methodology

BLOOD LEECH — feeds on other kindred Vitae rather than mortal blood. Distinctive Predator Type with sect-political consequences.
- Specialty: Brawl (Kindred) or Stealth (Against Kindred)
- Discipline: Celerity 1 or Protean 1
- Advantages: +1 Feeding capacity from kindred sources
- Flaws: -2 Humanity (chronicle-shaping ethical positioning); Dark Secret; chronicle-active threat from kindred who discover feeding pattern
- Suits: rare; chronicle-shaping when chosen; Banu Haqim-tradition concepts; certain Brisbane Sabbat-survivor diablerie-adjacent concepts
- Stains pattern: high Stains; the methodology is Tenet-violating in nearly all chronicles

CLEAVER — feeds from a controlled mortal household or family. Maintains the household as feeding ground; vessels rotate, kindred remains present.
- Specialty: Persuasion (Coercion) or Subterfuge (Maintaining Cover)
- Discipline: Dominate 1 or Presence 1
- Advantages: +2 Herd (the household); +1 Domain (the household's territory)
- Flaws: Dark Secret (the household's true nature); chronicle-active risk if household members organise resistance
- Suits: Camarilla orthodox stable-feeding concepts, methuselah-tempo Sydney private-household concepts, certain Hecata family family-tradition concepts
- Stains pattern: moderate Stains; long-term coercive relationship produces ongoing ethical pressure

CONSENSUALIST — feeds with vessel consent and awareness. Negotiated feeding arrangements; vessels accept feeding in exchange for protection, money, or relationship.
- Specialty: Persuasion (Seduction) or Medicine (Phlebotomy)
- Discipline: Auspex 1 or Fortitude 1
- Advantages: +1 Herd (consenting); +1 Humanity (consent-tradition feeding produces ethical anchor)
- Flaws: -1 Resources (consensual arrangements often costly to maintain)
- Suits: Anarch Movement Touchstone-rich concepts, methuselah-tempo Sydney aesthetic concepts (Sarrasine-tradition favours consensual aesthetics), Camarilla orthodox aristocratic concepts with consensual-tradition households
- Stains pattern: low Stains; consent-tradition reduces ethical violation

FARMER — feeds exclusively from animals rather than human vessels. Distinctive methodology with significant mechanical consequence.
- Specialty: Animal Ken (specific species) or Survival (Hunting)
- Discipline: Animalism 1 or Protean 1
- Advantages: +1 Humanity (animal-feeding tradition produces ethical anchor)
- Flaws: Feeding produces less Hunger reduction per session; Farming requires more time and effort; -2 to Hunger reduction rolls (a chronicle-active mechanical cost)
- Suits: chronicle-active ethical concepts; Salubri-tradition; Gangrel-tradition wilderness concepts; certain Hecata-family-tradition concepts
- Stains pattern: minimal Stains from feeding; chronicle-active mechanical cost compensates

OSIRIS — feeds from devoted mortal followers within a constructed mystique or cult-tradition relationship. Vessels worship or revere the kindred and offer themselves for feeding.
- Specialty: Performance (specific) or Subterfuge (False Religion)
- Discipline: Blood Sorcery 1 or Presence 1
- Advantages: +3 Herd (devoted followers); +1 Fame (within constructed cult-tradition)
- Flaws: Enemy (the dispossessed or the discoverer); chronicle-active Masquerade pressure from cult-tradition visibility
- Suits: Ministry-tradition concepts, Toreador aesthetic-tradition concepts, certain methuselah-tempo Sydney aesthetic-cult concepts, some Tremere-tradition concepts
- Stains pattern: moderate Stains; followers consent in some senses but are coerced in others

SANDMAN — feeds from sleeping vessels broken into. Stealth-focused; vessels often do not remember feeding occurred.
- Specialty: Stealth (Break-Ins) or Larceny (Lockpicking)
- Discipline: Obfuscate 1 or Auspex 1
- Advantages: +1 Resolve (focused practice); -1 Hunger increase rate per Sandman session (mechanical reward for stealth-feeding)
- Flaws: Masquerade pressure if break-in pattern detected; low mortal-network density (Sandman PCs often don't maintain vessel relationships)
- Suits: Nosferatu-tradition concepts, Obfuscate-heavy concepts, certain Camarilla orthodox stealth-tradition concepts
- Stains pattern: low Stains from per-feeding ethical violation; chronicle-active Masquerade pressure produces other Tenets pressure

SCENE QUEEN — feeds within a specific subculture, club scene, or social scene. Vessels are scene-participants; methodology is high-visibility but scene-protected.
- Specialty: Etiquette (Scene Protocol) or Persuasion (Scene Members)
- Discipline: Dominate 1 or Presence 1
- Advantages: +1 Fame (within scene); +1 Status (within Anarch or scene-tradition)
- Flaws: Beacon (visible to mortal authorities); -1 Status outside scene
- Suits: Anarch Movement Footscray Crew scene-embedded concepts (queer nightclub scenes, punk scenes, music scenes); methuselah-tempo Sydney aesthetic-scene concepts; certain Toreador-tradition concepts
- Stains pattern: moderate Stains; scene-tradition reduces ethical violation through scene-norms; chronicle-active Masquerade pressure

SIREN — feeds via seduction and intimate encounters. Vessels enter willingly; relationships are constructed but consensual within the feeding-context.
- Specialty: Persuasion (Seduction) or Subterfuge (Seduction Cover)
- Discipline: Presence 1 or Fortitude 1
- Advantages: Looks (Beautiful) Merit; +1 Herd (lovers)
- Flaws: Enemy (jealous mortal); chronicle-active mortal-relationship complications
- Suits: Toreador-tradition concepts, methuselah-tempo Sydney aesthetic-seduction concepts, certain Camarilla orthodox aristocratic-tradition concepts
- Stains pattern: low-to-moderate Stains; consent-tradition within seduction reduces ethical violation

EXTORTIONIST — feeds through coerced mortal arrangements; vessels comply under duress (debt, blackmail, threat).
- Specialty: Intimidation (Coercion) or Persuasion (Coercion)
- Discipline: Dominate 1 or Potence 1
- Advantages: +2 Resources (extorted wealth); +1 Contacts (criminal network)
- Flaws: Enemy (resentful vessels or their associates); chronicle-active mortal-resistance threat
- Suits: Anarch Movement criminal-tradition concepts, Brisbane Sabbat-survivor cell concepts, certain Camarilla orthodox enforcer concepts
- Stains pattern: high Stains; coercion-tradition is Tenet-violating in most chronicles

GRAVEROBBER — feeds from recently-dead bodies (within hours of death) or terminal-condition mortals near death.
- Specialty: Medicine (Cadavers) or Occult (Death Lore)
- Discipline: Fortitude 1 or Oblivion 1
- Advantages: +1 Herd (mortuary / hospice network); +1 Iron Gullet (can feed from low-quality blood sources)
- Flaws: Repulsive feeding pattern (-1 Social with non-Hecata kindred); -1 Status
- Suits: Hecata family family-tradition concepts (the methodology aligns with Hecata Painful Kiss Bane and Morbidity Compulsion); certain Gangrel-tradition wilderness concepts; rare in other clans
- Stains pattern: low Stains from direct feeding (vessels often unconscious or dead); chronicle-active ethical positioning

ROADSIDE KILLER — feeds from transient strangers in remote or isolated locations. Highway, motel-tradition, transient-mortal concepts.
- Specialty: Drive (Long-Distance) or Stealth (Wilderness)
- Discipline: Fortitude 1 or Protean 1
- Advantages: +1 Survival; chronicle-active itinerant capacity
- Flaws: Enemy (a federal investigator or hunter-tradition figure tracking the pattern); -1 Domain stability
- Suits: Ravnos-tradition concepts, Gangrel wilderness concepts, certain Brisbane Sabbat-survivor cell-operative concepts
- Stains pattern: moderate Stains; vessel-death pattern often produces chronicle-active investigation pressure

MONTERO — feeds via hunting parties and organised pursuit. Vessels are hunted (often consensually within Sabbat-tradition or aristocratic-tradition hunting parties).
- Specialty: Leadership (Hunt Coordination) or Survival (Tracking)
- Discipline: Dominate 1 or Obfuscate 1
- Advantages: +2 Retainers (hunt party); +1 Domain (hunting grounds)
- Flaws: Enemy (escaped quarry or families of quarry); chronicle-active hunting-pattern Masquerade pressure
- Suits: Brisbane Sabbat-survivor pack-tradition concepts; Ventrue-tradition aristocratic-hunt concepts; rare in modern chronicles
- Stains pattern: high Stains; hunting-as-feeding methodology is chronicle-shaping ethical positioning

PURSUER — feeds from carefully-selected individual vessels tracked, hunted, and engaged across extended time. Vessel selection is deliberate; the relationship is predatory but personalised.
- Specialty: Investigation (Stalking) or Stealth (Shadowing)
- Discipline: Auspex 1 or Obfuscate 1
- Advantages: +1 Bloodhound (Auspex-adjacent ability to track vessels by scent / blood-trace)
- Flaws: Enemy (former vessel who survived and remembers); chronicle-active investigation pressure
- Suits: Malkavian-tradition concepts, certain Auspex-heavy concepts; rare elsewhere
- Stains pattern: moderate-to-high Stains; personalised predation produces ongoing ethical pressure

TRAPDOOR — feeds via a specific feeding-ground location (an apartment, a club booth, a private room) where vessels are lured. Lair-tradition predation.
- Specialty: Larceny (Trap Construction) or Persuasion (Luring)
- Discipline: Obfuscate 1 or Protean 1
- Advantages: +2 Haven (the feeding-ground); +1 Domain
- Flaws: Trapped Haven (the feeding-ground can be discovered and turned against the PC); -1 Stealth outside trapdoor location
- Suits: Nosferatu-tradition lair concepts, certain Tzimisce-tradition haven concepts, methuselah-tempo Sydney private-audience concepts (Sarrasine herself operates trapdoor-adjacent feeding methodology)
- Stains pattern: moderate Stains; methodology produces vessel-pattern consistency that may be Tenet-violating

PREDATOR TYPE SELECTION GUIDANCE:

- Match to character concept: a coterie's investigator-PC suits Pursuer or Bagger; an aesthetic-PC suits Siren or Scene Queen; a cell-operative PC suits Alleycat or Extortionist.
- Match to chronicle mode: Camarilla orthodox favours Cleaver, Consensualist, Siren, Osiris (stable-feeding methodologies); Anarch Movement favours Scene Queen, Consensualist, Alleycat; Brisbane Sabbat-survivor favours Alleycat, Extortionist, Roadside Killer (cell-tradition methodologies); methuselah-tempo Sydney favours Siren, Consensualist, Osiris, Trapdoor (aesthetic-tradition methodologies); Hecata favours Graverobber, Bagger (family-tradition methodologies); cross-supernatural diplomatic favours Consensualist, Sandman (low-Masquerade-pressure methodologies).
- Match to coterie ethical register: Touchstone-rich coteries struggle with high-Stains Predator Types; low-Humanity-tolerance coteries accommodate Alleycat, Extortionist, Roadside Killer; high-Humanity-pursuit coteries favour Consensualist, Farmer, Bagger.
- Match to Predator-Type Discipline bonus: if PC wants Celerity, Predator Types granting Celerity (Alleycat, Blood Leech) align; if PC wants Dominate, Predator Types granting Dominate (Bagger, Cleaver, Extortionist, Montero, Scene Queen) align.

KIT NOTES:

- Predator Type selection often shapes chronicle-active mortal-network: a Cleaver's household, a Scene Queen's scene, a Siren's lover network, a Pursuer's tracked vessels are all chronicle-active recurring NPCs.
- Some Predator Types (Blood Leech, Montero, Extortionist) are chronicle-shaping when chosen; Storytellers should confirm at session zero that the chronicle can absorb high-Stains methodology PCs.
- Some Predator Types (Farmer, Consensualist) shape character Humanity baseline and chronicle-active ethical register; coteries with all-Farmer or all-Consensualist PCs produce different chronicle tenor than mixed-methodology coteries.
- Thin-Blood Alchemy PCs have variant Predator Type options reflecting Thin-Blood physiology (less reliable feeding, daywalking-tradition feeding patterns) — consult Storyteller for Thin-Blood-specific Predator Type handling.

GENERATION AND BLOOD POTENCY

Generation measures the kindred's distance from Caine, the legendary first kindred. Lower generation = closer to Caine = more powerful blood, more potent Disciplines, slower Bane manifestation, more Hunger-related restrictions on feeding sources.

Generation ranges:
- 1st Generation: Caine
- 2nd-3rd Generation: Antediluvians (the clan founders)
- 4th-5th Generation: methuselah-tempo kindred (Sarrasine is 5th-6th gen, 1,470-year tenure)
- 6th-8th Generation: elder kindred (Lytton is 7th gen, 136-year tenure; Octavia Marsh is 7th gen, 132 years; Bishop Callista Vox is 7th gen, 213 years)
- 9th-11th Generation: established kindred
- 12th-13th Generation: neonate kindred (typical PC range)
- 14th-16th Generation: Thin-Blood

KIT PC GENERATION DEFAULTS:

- 13th Generation: standard PC default. Most kit PCs are 13th gen.
- 12th Generation: slightly-more-established PCs; mid-career neonates.
- 11th Generation: established-coterie chronicles; PCs with significant Embrace-tradition history.
- 10th Generation: rare; chronicle-shaping; requires Storyteller approval and chronicle frame justification.
- 9th and lower: not standard PC range; reserved for Storyteller NPCs.

BLOOD POTENCY:

Blood Potency is the mechanical measure of Vitae power, ranging 0-10. It governs:

- HUNGER COST per Discipline use (higher Blood Potency = higher Hunger cost for activations)
- BANE SEVERITY (higher Blood Potency = stronger Bane manifestation)
- FEEDING POOL SIZE (higher Blood Potency = larger Hunger pool, more difficult to satisfy from mortal feeding)
- FEEDING SOURCE RESTRICTIONS (high Blood Potency Kindred cannot satisfy Hunger from animal blood, then cannot satisfy from non-human mortal blood, etc.)
- DISCIPLINE POWER MAXIMUMS (Blood Potency caps maximum Discipline rating for that PC)

BLOOD POTENCY BY GENERATION (standard kit values):

- 16th-14th Gen (Thin-Blood): Blood Potency 0
- 13th Gen: Blood Potency 1 (default for most PCs)
- 12th Gen: Blood Potency 1
- 11th Gen: Blood Potency 2
- 10th Gen: Blood Potency 2-3
- 9th Gen: Blood Potency 3
- 8th Gen: Blood Potency 3-4
- 7th Gen: Blood Potency 4-5 (elder kindred tier; Lytton, Octavia, Bishop Callista)
- 6th-5th Gen: Blood Potency 5-6 (methuselah-tempo tier; Sarrasine, Cardinals)
- 4th-3rd Gen: Blood Potency 7-9 (Antediluvian tier; not chronicle-active)

KIT STARTING BLOOD POTENCY:

- Most neonate PCs (13th gen): Blood Potency 1
- Mid-career PCs (12th gen): Blood Potency 1
- Established-tradition PCs (11th gen): Blood Potency 2
- Higher Blood Potency requires Storyteller approval and chronicle-frame justification

BLOOD POTENCY EFFECTS AT VARIOUS RATINGS:

Blood Potency 0 (Thin-Blood): no Bane Severity; full feeding source flexibility; Discipline access limited to Thin-Blood Alchemy.

Blood Potency 1: Bane Severity 1 (minimal); feeding from any human is satisfying; Discipline ratings cap at 4.

Blood Potency 2: Bane Severity 1; feeding from any human is satisfying; Hunger pool size 1; Discipline ratings cap at 4.

Blood Potency 3: Bane Severity 2; cannot feed from animal blood for satisfaction; Hunger pool larger; Discipline ratings cap at 5.

Blood Potency 4: Bane Severity 2; cannot feed from animal blood; can drink only from healthy adults; Hunger pool larger; Discipline ratings cap at 5; Disciplines cost +1 Hunger to activate certain powers.

Blood Potency 5: Bane Severity 3; can only drink from very specific human types (the Storyteller defines per Generation tradition; methuselah-tempo); Discipline ratings cap at 6; chronicle-active feeding-pressure produced by Blood Potency itself.

Blood Potency 6+: methuselah-tempo and above; chronicle-shaping feeding patterns; specific vessel-tradition required; Discipline ratings 6+ accessible; chronicle-active feeding-difficulty pressure.

GENERATION-RELATED ADVANTAGES AND FLAWS:

GENERATION as Advantage: rare; some chronicles allow PCs to spend Advantage points to lower Generation by one (13th → 12th gen, etc.). Storyteller approval required.

THIN-BLOOD FLAW: standard for Thin-Blood PCs; baseline.

DARK SECRET (GENERATION): PCs whose Generation is higher than they admit (claiming 12th gen while actually 13th-14th) face chronicle-active Masquerade pressure if discovered.

DIABLERIE-DERIVED GENERATION: PCs who have committed diablerie (consuming another kindred's soul) and gained Generation reduction face Auspex-detection vulnerability for 5-15 years post-diablerie; chronicle-shaping ethical positioning.

KIT NOTES:

- Default kit chronicle PCs are 13th generation, Blood Potency 1. This is the standard.
- Camarilla orthodox Melbourne chronicles occasionally include 11th-12th gen PCs reflecting longer Embrace-tradition history; Lytton's court has documented neonate-to-13th-generation Embrace pattern across the past 50 years.
- Brisbane Sabbat-survivor cells occasionally include 11th gen PCs from pre-Gehenna-War Sabbat-tradition Embrace lineages; cell-tradition stability has preserved some lower-gen presence.
- Methuselah-tempo Sydney coteries are typically 13th gen (Sarrasine selects junior kindred deliberately; lower-generation kindred in her domain operate independently of the audience structure).
- Anarch Movement Footscray Crew coteries are typically 13th-14th gen and Thin-Blood; Movement-tradition embraces working-class and recent-Embrace kindred.
- Hecata family Calabria Branch coteries vary; family-tradition Embrace patterns sometimes produce 11th-12th gen PCs reflecting branch's longer tradition; chronicle-active.
- Cross-supernatural diplomatic Cress Truce coteries are typically 12th-13th gen; framework-tradition prefers established-but-not-elder kindred for negotiation work.

GENERATION AND BLOOD POTENCY ARE MOSTLY FIXED:

Generation almost never changes (diablerie is the rare exception); Blood Potency can rise over centuries of unlife but not within most chronicle scopes. PCs are working with their starting Generation and Blood Potency across the chronicle. Plan character mechanically accordingly.
